$comment: Global rules for the weightage layer. Weightage never modifies the syllabus: it references syllabus IDs (exam/stage/section/topic/subtopic).

basisLegend.official-marks: Derived arithmetically from official marks in the notification (e.g. section marks ÷ stage marks). The only basis with isOfficial = true.
basisLegend.pyq-estimate: Estimate informed by secondary previous-year question analyses listed in evidence.json (candidate-recall based, not official).
basisLegend.proxy-estimate: No PYQ data for this exam/section; borrowed from a structurally similar exam's PYQ data (named in the justification).
basisLegend.editorial-estimate: No PYQ data found; judgement based on syllabus scope and typical question styles. Lowest reliability.
basisLegend.nominal: No marks attached (qualifying/pass-fail test) or single-topic section; weight assigned only so the hierarchy is complete.
basisLegend.custom: Set by the user via the `custom` field; overrides `default`.

confidenceLegend.medium: Multiple shifts/years of secondary topic-wise analysis agree.
confidenceLegend.low: Single source, single shift, or aggregator ranges without stated basis.
confidenceLegend.very-low: Proxy or editorial estimate; no direct historical data.

stageWeighting.rule: Within a track, each scored stage's weight = its maximum marks ÷ total maximum marks of the track's scored stages. Pass/fail stages (PST/PET, medical, personality test, local-language test) are gates with weight 0.
stageWeighting.note: Prelims are weighted even though their marks are not added to final merit, because they must be cleared competitively (cut-offs).

meritRatios.$comment: Where the notification states how merit stages combine, the marks share of those stages is split by the official ratio instead of raw marks.

ibps-po.source: ibps-po-xvi-2026-notice, J. Interview: 'relative weightage of Online Main Exam and interview will be 80:20'

ibps-rrb-po.source: ibps-rrb-xv-2026-notice, J. Interview: 'weightage of Online Examination and Interview will be 80:20'

sbi-po.source: sbi-po-2026-advt, Final Selection: Main 230 → 75, GE & Interview 50 → 25

nonAcademicSubjects.note: Interview, psychometric, physical and skill/language tests are weighted and prioritised like any topic, but listed separately from academic top-10 tables.

sectionWeighting.rule: Section weight = section marks ÷ stage marks. Sections in the same choiceGroup are alternatives: each gets the full group weight, and the group is counted once in the 100% total. Sections with no marks are gates (weight 0). If no section in a stage has marks, weights are split equally (nominal).

topicWeighting.rule: Each topic has an expected question range [min, max] per paper. Default weight = midpoint ÷ sum of midpoints × 100, rounded to 2 decimals (largest-remainder, so the section totals exactly 100.00).
topicWeighting.trendRule: consistent if min > 0 and (max − min) ≤ 0.34 × max; fluctuating if min = 0 or the spread is larger; explicit trend tags (emerging/declining/new-pattern) override.

subtopicWeighting.rule: Relative importance profile per topic (SSC or banking variant), renormalised over the subtopics the exam includes, rounded to 2 decimals summing to 100.00.

priority.rule: Within an exam track, topics are sorted by effective overall weight (descending). Topics whose cumulative share reaches the threshold fall in that band; the topic that crosses a threshold stays in the higher band.
priority.gateRule: Topics that only appear in pass/fail gates (weight 0) get 'High': failing them eliminates the candidate regardless of marks.

rules: Every track's stage weights total 100 (gate stages are 0).
Every stage's section weights total 100 (choice groups counted once; alternatives must carry equal weight).
Every syllabus stage, section, topic and subtopic has exactly one weightage entry; no orphans, no duplicates.
Weights are within 0–100; basis, confidence and priority values are from the legends; lastUpdated is an ISO date.
